subject: R82 E2-E3-X01-X03-S01-S05 optimized joint-tail and apparent floor sensitivity implementations

findings.finding: Working q_app source ratio from a 2048-row 4-window shared CF4 cohort must not be promoted to physical x_C/U_sigma or nine independent Planck maps. Original S02 unknown physical Q/F/GF mass is 1.
findings.fix: Typed 0/1/2 known/missing codes, conditional event bounds, shared sample IDs and physical_Pi=None. R78 science gates unchanged.
findings.evidence: C7_SOURCE_REPLAY.json and source P1 arrays, original X03 retrospective ledger

findings.finding: Naive per-threshold source scan O(N*T) was slower than sorting 6 weighted one-dimensional event score arrays O(6NlogN+6TlogN). C++ OpenMP also slower than sorted NumPy on original 2048-row source.
findings.fix: Production NumPy reference changed to stable argsort+reverse weighted survival+searchsorted(side=right), handling unknowns through ±inf; C++ optional disabled by default.
findings.red: Observed test failure: expected numpy_sorted_reference, got original numpy_reference
findings.green: 20 new R82 tests passed; 228 wide tests passed

findings.finding: Anchor*floor may silently underflow to zero or overflow to infinity although both factors are finite positive, inducing invalid ratio.
findings.fix: Reject invalid product before either NumPy or Fortran execution; preserve exact strict ties and nonnegative amplitude domain.
findings.red: Existing pre-fix floor product cases did not raise
findings.green: Finite positive product test, floor original S03 6-grid parity, 228 wide tests passed

findings.finding: Historical E2/X01/X02/X03 source hashes keyed by node ID are not filesystem paths. Original C7 result had mixed key semantics and the first replay script failed.
findings.fix: Separate source file path SHA dictionary from historical_sha_by_node_id; compare both with original existing files and source provenance.
findings.evidence: C7_SOURCE_REPLAY.json and verify_original.py, no physical data changed

findings.finding: Fortran 8-worker floor-grid is faster than both original NumPy and chunked NumPy on actual 32x24 and 64x64 source grids, with <2e-11 errors.
findings.fix: Certify Fortran default auto above threshold; C++ optional source-SHA-checked, NumPy sorted default for tails; do not claim end-to-end speedup.
